Thought: In order to solve this problem, I need to determine which nuclei have a magnetic moment and are suitable for NMR (Nuclear Magnetic Resonance) experiments. Typically, nuclei with an odd mass number or an odd atomic number have a non-zero nuclear spin, which gives them a magnetic moment suitable for NMR.

- ^{12}C has an even mass number and atomic number, so it has no nuclear spin.
- ^{14}N has an odd atomic number, which means it has a nuclear spin and, therefore, a magnetic moment.
- ^{16}O has even mass and atomic numbers, indicating it has no nuclear spin and no magnetic moment.
- ^{32}S has even mass and atomic numbers, so it also has no nuclear spin and no magnetic moment.

Based on this analysis, ^{14}N is the nucleus with a magnetic moment suitable for NMR experiments.
